summary: Answered the audit's last open half from the shipped storage implementation rather than leaving it as an unexamined unknown, and recorded the storage behaviour itself. MemoryStorage::get_entries and get_suffix subtract self.trimmed_idx from the caller's index without a guard (memory_storage.rs 92-107) and trim does the same (122-127), so a caller that asks for a prefix below the trimmed index gets one of exactly two outcomes depending on the build: under overflow checks - the profile every receipt in this run was compiled with, per the recorded cargo artifacts - the subtraction panics, and with overflow checks disabled it wraps past the end of the log and the read returns an empty vector, which is the silently empty suffix the gap named. Because the Storage trait leaves out-of-range behaviour to the implementer, that answer belongs to the implementation and the profile rather than to the library, and it is source-derived: no run asked the storage for a prefix below a compacted index. The trim child's account was rewritten as a successor that carries this three-part split of its gap - in-cluster route executed and silent, truthful-peer route closed by source through the per-node initialisation of the recorded accepted vector, storage-level route answered for the shipped implementation - with its answer, counterevidence, limitations and knowledge uses updated, and a new knowledge entry records the memory-storage behaviour. Incomplete by design and now stated as such in the record: the gap stays unresolved because no execution covers the storage-level case and other implementations or build profiles may behave differently, and the forwarded-compaction peer sampling and the delivery of a Snapshot compaction to a NoSnapshot instance remain unexecuted. This closes the turn; the run's accounts are current, internally consistent, and each names its own evidence and its own limits.
